_comment: Corpora for scripts/corpus-bench.js. Chosen to span the project shapes CodeSeeker claims to support, not to be easy. The RealWorld implementations are the canonical cross-stack reference app, so the same domain appears in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python — which isolates language handling from domain difficulty. Absent paths are skipped with a notice rather than failing the run.

corpora.name: realworld-react-redux
corpora.why: The shape reported in issue #5 — JavaScript, flat layout, no TypeScript. Graph coverage was reported short here and has never been verified.

corpora.name: realworld-node-express
corpora.why: Server-side JavaScript with CommonJS-style module resolution — the other half of the issue #5 hypothesis.

corpora.name: realworld-django
corpora.why: Python is claimed as wired Tree-sitter support. The claim has never been measured on a real corpus.

corpora.name: codeseeker-self
corpora.why: The reference case. Everything measured during development was measured here, so it is the control, not the evidence.

corpora.name: pragmaworks
corpora.why: Our own, and the GS reference project — the exemplar CodeSeeker's own specification was modelled on.

corpora.name: chronicle
corpora.why: Our own. Sibling architecture, independent codebase.

corpora.name: forge
corpora.why: Scale. Everything else here is under 600 files; indexing cost and graph integrity at 2485 is a different regime.

corpora.name: realworld-aspnetcore
corpora.shape: ASP.NET Core API, MediatR handlers, EF Core
corpora.why: C# is claimed as supported with a regex parser and has never been measured on a real corpus. The same Conduit domain as the other RealWorld entries, so a score gap here is language handling rather than task difficulty.
